question: Estimate Punctual Pros revenue from public filings
html:
Punctual Pros' FY2025 pro forma revenue is about $22M est. (range $16–28M), including the Horvath Home Services add-on in New Jersey. Confidence is medium. Two independent methods support it: a payroll build-up and a franchise-disclosure mapping (Punctual Pros public filings).

How the estimate is built

  • Payroll anchor. The Rohrer Company's April 2020 PPP loan of $745,985 implies ~$3.58M of 2019 payroll. That points to ~50–58 employees and ~$9–12M of 2019 revenue est. Revenue confidence is low (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Growth to the deal. Headcount of ~113 by 2024 roughly doubles that base. At ~$76K Lancaster wages and a 40–45% labor ratio, it supports a PA run-rate of ~$18–22M est. at BSP's Apr 3, 2024 entry. The 113 figure is not re-verified (BSP firm profile).
  • Franchise disclosure check. The 2026 franchisee lists show 25 territories. Mapping them to Item 19 quartiles gives ~$12–19M est. for PA and ~$3–5M est. for NJ in FY2025 (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Add-on base. Horvath's PPP loan of $251,894 implies ~19–22 staff and ~$3–4M of 2019 revenue est. (Punctual Pros public filings).

Estimate summary

MetricEstimateConfidence
FY2025 PA revenue~$18M est. ($12–24M)Medium
FY2025 NJ revenue~$3–5M est.Medium
FY2025 pro forma total~$22M est. ($16–28M)Medium
Revenue per territory~$0.9M est.Low
Adjusted EBITDA~$1.8–3.1M est. (central ~$2.6M)Low

Signals worth testing

  • Territory productivity. Revenue per territory of ~$0.9M est. is above system averages of $0.61–0.66M for One Hour and Ben Franklin. Either the operations outperform, or the PA estimate is high (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Margin ceiling. Royalty plus brand fund takes ~7.2–7.5% of revenue, about $1.6M a year est. That caps adjusted EBITDA margins at about 8–14% est. (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Leverage. PGIM Private Credit Fund's Jun 30, 2026 10-Q shows a first-lien loan to Punctual Pros Midco at SOFR + 5.00% (8.73%), maturing Mar 26, 2029. Terms are:
  • $4.83M funded, marked at ~98.6% of par.
  • A $1.4M unfunded commitment.

The modest funded debt is consistent with a low-$20M revenue business (Punctual Pros public filings).

Gaps in the data

  • There is no audited or management revenue. The range would narrow with trailing twelve-month revenue by territory and brand, plus current payroll registers.
  • The share of revenue from the NJ add-on after close is inferred. Horvath's post-close financials would answer it.
  • The filings were spot-checked on Sep 24, 2026. Of 30 items sampled, 29 were confirmed and 1 was removed (Punctual Pros public filings).

Next actions

  1. Reconcile the ~$22M est. against management's FY2025 revenue by brand and state. Document the variance by method.
  2. Pull royalty and brand-fund remittances to back-solve gross revenue precisely.
  3. Benchmark revenue per territory against Item 19 quartiles. Confirm whether outperformance is real before using it in the growth plan.
  4. Refresh the leverage view when PGIM's next 10-Q posts, including any draw on the $1.4M commitment.
